body:
Binary inputs previously selected Gists solely by size, and repository uploads always staged `.log.txt` files. This adds `gh-upload` for universal uploads while continuing releases of `gh-upload-log` with the same version and code.

- Both npm packages ship the `gh-upload` and `gh-upload-log` commands; `uploadFile` aliases the existing `uploadLog` API. New `GH_UPLOAD_*` settings support the legacy configuration names.
- Complete UTF-8 validation selects readable text or streaming gzip archives. Actual compressed bytes, including archive overhead, are split into parts of at most 100 MB. Existing text line/UTF-8 splitting, repository targets, retries, resumption, and deduplication remain supported.
- Per-name manifests and uncached exact-version checks make publication resumable. GitHub release outputs are set only after both package versions are visible on npm, with up to five minutes of visibility polling after each successful publish. Changeset helpers and release badges use the manifest names; one minor changeset prepares 0.11.0.
- README recovery instructions, a universal upload example, and repeatable investigation/round-trip probes are included.

Reproduce the original binary routing problem with:

```bash
node -e "require('node:fs').writeFileSync('/tmp/issue-37.bin', Buffer.from([0,255,128,10]))"
bun src/cli.js /tmp/issue-37.bin --dry-mode --verbose
```

Previously this selected a Gist. It now selects repository mode and reports a gzip archive; forcing `--only-gist` rejects the binary before GitHub commands. The initial automated regressions failed **0 passing / 13 failing** before implementation; [preserved reproduction and investigation](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-upload-log/blob/issue-37-663142bb0564/docs/case-studies/issue-37/README.md).

Validation:

- [CI run 37770722396](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-upload-log/actions/runs/37770722396) passes on commit `40a7753`: changeset validation, lint/formatting, and Bun tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- `bun test`: **181 passing, 0 failing**, including binary reconstruction, archive overhead, hundreds of ordered parts, long filenames, CLI compatibility, changeset merging, and publication failures/visibility delays.
- `bun run check`: ESLint, Prettier and the 1000-line source limit pass; `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes. Changeset validation passes against the actual base/head commits.
- Real Git integration interrupts and resumes an archive with a different chunk size, reconstructs its exact bytes, preserves existing files/main, and deduplicates the next upload.
- A finite **104,923,136-byte** random input reconstructed with the same SHA-256 from parts of **104,857,600** and **97,579 bytes**, under a 192 MB V8 heap limit ([result](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-upload-log/blob/issue-37-663142bb0564/docs/case-studies/issue-37/large-roundtrip.json)).
- Both planned **0.11.0** artifacts passed npm packing, local installation, API import, both installed command checks, and npm dry-publication ([results](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-upload-log/blob/issue-37-663142bb0564/docs/case-studies/issue-37/package-smoke.json)).

Release prerequisite: uncached registry checks found both candidate name families and their punctuation variants absent, and the new name passed dry publication. No real npm publication was performed. The first `gh-upload` publication needs npm browser authorization, followed by package-specific trust for `release.yml`. A maintainer can bootstrap the pushed PR with `package-registry-manager setup --repository /path/to/gh-upload-log --registry npm --package gh-upload --ref 51 --execute`; the README documents this setup. Both packages must have trusted publishers configured before automatic releases.

The optional `gh-upload-image` policy-only probe returned HTTP 422/HTML with current authentication and uploaded no image. Its end-to-end asset backend remains unverified, so images use the tested gzip repository path.

Closes #37.
title: feat: publish gh-upload and support binary file archives
